page.layout: Running head across top: EMBLEMATA, page number 124 at top right. Full-width heading line: "Homo coelum versus spuens." with "XXIIII." at right. Below: one woodcut emblem picture (no text in it). Below the picture: a verse epigram of four lines in italic with large initial C, full width.

main_text.head: Homo coelum versus spuens. XXIIII.
main_text.p: CErnis ut hic coelum fædo qui conspuit ore, Non coelum,imò suos conspuit ipse sinus ? Et tu cælorum Domini contemptor,in illum Non quod Verba iacis,tot tibi probra vomis ?

page.notes: The woodcut shows a man in a landscape with a castle and trees, spitting upward toward the sky. The large initial C is a decorative letter. Note the long s in the verse is printed as f-like s and has been rendered as s. Some words in the verse ("Cernis", "Verba", "vomis") have the first letter in a decorative form; read as printed.
